function.name: dynamic_pricing_calculate
function.description: Calculate the dynamic price for a product based on the IP address of the customer while ensuring the price does not fall below a minimum floor value. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

ip_address.description: The IP address of the customer, used to determine the geographical location for pricing adjustments.

base_price.description: The base price of the product before dynamic adjustments. This is a float type value.

price_floor.description: The minimum allowable price for the product after dynamic adjustments. This is a float type value.

pricing_factor.description: A multiplier based on the customer's location, used to adjust the base price dynamically. This is a float type value.

message.content:
### 1. Start With Your Cost & Value Lens  

| Item | Why It Matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Cost‑to‑Serve** | Know your fixed & variable costs per filing (staff, software, compliance). This sets the *minimum* you can charge without losing money. |
| **Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)** | Estimate how many filings a typical customer will do over their relationship. If a customer stays 2 years and does 5 filings per year, CLV ≈ 5 × average margin. |
| **Competitive Position** | You’re in a commodity space, so differentiation comes from *speed*, *accuracy*, *support*, or *bundled services*. |

> **Rule of thumb:** Price ≥ 2 × cost per filing + a margin that reflects the perceived value.  
> For example, if it costs $30 to process a filing, a healthy margin would be $60–$80 per filing.

---

### 2. Define Your Target Segments  

| Segment | Typical Needs | Pricing Implication |
|---------|---------------|---------------------|
| **Solo/Small Firms** | One or two filings a year, minimal support | Offer a low‑entry “Starter” plan ($99–$119) that covers 1–2 filings. |
| **Mid‑Size Firms** | 3–10 filings/year, want predictable budgeting | Annual subscription ($149–$179) that includes unlimited filings + priority support. |
| **Large Enterprises** | 20+ filings/year, require custom integrations | Enterprise tier ($299+) with volume discounts, dedicated account manager, SLA guarantees. |

> **Tip:** Use *tiered pricing* to capture different willingness‑to‑pay levels while keeping the core product identical.

---

### 3. Choose a Pricing Model That Fits the Commodity Nature  

| Model | How It Works | Pros | Cons |
|-------|--------------|------|------|
| **Flat‑Rate Subscription** | Fixed fee per year covering unlimited filings | Predictable revenue, easy to understand | May under‑charge high‑volume users |
| **Usage‑Based** | Pay per filing (e.g., $79 per filing) | Aligns price with value, scales with growth | Revenue volatility, harder to forecast |
| **Hybrid** | Base fee + per‑filing add‑on | Balances predictability & scalability | Slightly more complex to explain |

> **Recommendation:** Start with a **hybrid** model: $129/year for unlimited filings *plus* a small per‑filing fee ($9–$19) for extra filings beyond a baseline (e.g., first 12 filings free). This gives you a stable base while still capturing high‑volume customers.

---

### 4. Set the Numbers (Sample Pricing Grid)

| Plan | Features | Price |
|------|----------|-------|
| **Starter** | 1–2 filings/year, email support | **$99** (one‑time) |
| **Growth** | Unlimited filings, phone support, quarterly compliance updates | **$149** (annual) |
| **Pro** | Unlimited filings, 24/7 support, API access, custom reporting | **$199** (annual) |
| **Enterprise** | Unlimited filings, dedicated account manager, SLA 99.9%, custom integrations | **$299** (annual) |

> **Why these numbers?**  
> • $99 matches the lowest competitor’s one‑time offer but adds *value* (email support).  
> • $149 aligns with the mid‑tier competitor but positions you as the *cheaper* choice for unlimited filings.  
> • $199–$299 gives room for higher‑margin enterprise features.

---

### 5. Add Psychological & Strategic Touches  

| Tactic | How It Helps |
|--------|--------------|
| **Price Anchoring** | Show the “original” price ($149) next to the discounted $129 to create perceived savings. |
| **Bundling** | Bundle filings with optional add‑ons (e.g., expedited processing for $29). |
| **Limited‑Time Discounts** | Offer a 10% discount for the first 100 sign‑ups to generate urgency. |
| **Free Trial / Freemium** | Let prospects file 1–2 documents for free; upsell to paid tiers once they see the value. |

---

### 6. Test, Iterate, & Optimize  

1. **A/B Test** different price points for the same plan (e.g., $139 vs. $149).  
2. **Track Key Metrics**: CAC, churn rate, average revenue per user (ARPU), CLV.  
3. **Collect Feedback**: Ask why customers chose a particular plan; refine messaging accordingly.  
4. **Adjust Dynamically**: If you have a dynamic pricing engine, feed in real‑time data (competitor changes, demand spikes) to tweak prices within set bounds.

---

### 7. Quick Decision Matrix  

| Criterion | Weight | Competitor A | Competitor B | Your Suggested Price |
|-----------|--------|--------------|--------------|----------------------|
| **Base Cost Coverage** | 30% | $99 | $149 | $129 |
| **Unlimited Filings Value** | 25% | $149 | $249 | $149 |
| **Support Level** | 15% | Basic | Premium | Growth Tier |
| **Market Positioning** | 20% | Low | High | Mid‑Range |
| **Profit Margin** | 10% | 40% | 35% | 45% |

> **Result:** The hybrid $129–$149 range hits the sweet spot between cost coverage, competitive parity, and margin.

---

### Bottom Line  

- **Use a hybrid pricing model**: $129/year for unlimited filings + a modest per‑filing fee for extras.  
- **Offer tiered plans** that reflect varying support and feature needs.  
- **Leverage psychological pricing** (anchoring, bundling) to make the value clear.  
- **Iterate quickly**: run A/B tests, monitor metrics, and adjust as you learn what resonates with your target segments.

With this approach you’ll stay competitive against both $99 and $149 one‑time offers while building a sustainable recurring revenue stream.
